newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shrs surge to strong close on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Chile shrs surge to strong close on foreign buying.

text.p: Chilean stocks raged ahead to a record close on an influx of foreign capital and on confidence that a drought parching central Chile is now over, brokers said.

The blue-chip IPSA index smashed past the 130-point psychological barrier, retreating modestly late in the session on profit-taking, but still ending 2.14 percent higher for the day at 129.29 points, brokers said.
The all-share IGPA ended 1.61 percent higher at 5652.17 points on thumping volume of 220 million shares traded.
Expectations of low volume because of the Thursday holiday proved misplaced as foreign demand injected money into the market, buoying prices, brokers said.
"We're still a small market and when you get a foreigner sending down $100 million, we really feel it," said one broker. "What we had today was a strong movement from overseas."
Electrical shares, which often set the tempo for the Chilean market, were among the biggest gainers. Endesa was up 3.6 percent to 302 pesos, and Enersis rose 2.9 percent to 281 pesos.

Endesa and other hydroelectric power generators were among the most vulnerable to the water shortage that had afflicted central Chile. But steady rain since Wednesday has washed away drought concerns and the government said the rains ensure a steady supply of electricity at least until August.

Most reservoirs in central Chile are now at or above normal levels, said the National Energy Commission. Chile depends heavily on hydroelectric power and the drought had depressed electrical shares prices on concerns utilities would have to spend heavily on fossil fuels to make up for lower dam output.
Other gainers included Laboratorio Chile after its big stock auction on Wednesday, ending 5.3 percent higher at 516 pesos, and Santa Isabel, up 3.9 percent to 790 pesos.

The market was also buoyed by comments from Economy Minister Alvaro Garca, who said economic growth would continue strong to the end of the year. Second-half growth would be at least six percent, Garca said.
